title: The Space Story
intro: Our short explainer video introduces NASA's space hardware in plain language. It comes with captions, a full written transcript, an audio-described version and a sign-language video.
transcript: [A golden footpad on grey moon dust, beside a bootprint. A title reads: Mind my foot!]
Narrator: Mind my foot! You're standing on my footpad.
Narrator: I'm Eagle's descent stage.
Narrator: On the 20th of July, 1969, I burned for 756 seconds
[An astronaut stands by the lander's ladder.]
[The lander's engine fires, throwing up dust. A fuel gauge reads seven percent.]
Narrator: to land two humans at Tranquility Base.
[The gauge falls to zero, empty.]
Narrator: Engineers gave me four legs, a ladder, and room to carry science. And no seats.
[A cartoon armchair appears beside the cramped lander.]
Narrator: Talk about standing room only.
Narrator: After 21 hours, Eagle's top half launched from my back.
[Two astronauts stand on the Moon, with Earth in the black sky. They wave, and one gives a thumbs up.]
Narrator: I stayed behind.
Narrator: 17 meters away, my little sibling, EASEP,
[A small solar-powered science station sits on the surface, rings of light pulsing outward.]
Narrator: listened for tremors in the Moon.
Narrator: It measured dust, powered by the sun.
[A thermometer shows plus thirty degrees Celsius.]
Narrator: It even survived heat 30 degrees past plan.
Narrator: Then, on the 27th of August, it stopped answering.
[It goes dark. A calendar shows the 27th of August, 1969.]
[A panel of mirrors glints in the sunlight.]
Narrator: Five meters away, a reflector needs no power at all.
[The lander stands far behind, the small reflector in front.]
Narrator: Keep waiting. Come say hi.
[The Moon fills the screen, with the Earth beside it among the stars.]
